A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spec-VLA work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including v2's added Appendix C.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original LIBERO simulation results, including task success, decoding speed, threshold ablations and acceptance-length analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original LIBERO experiments and adds quantization timing results in Appendix C, Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The Llama-layer draft model, visual/textual feature fusion, Eagle-2 draft tree and bin-distance acceptance rule remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. Appendix C evaluates precision configurations without documenting a revised Spec-VLA algorithm or training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use LIBERO-Goal, Object, Spatial and Long, with the same task coverage. Appendix C reuses these suites at different numerical precisions; no new dataset, task or robot environment is evaluated.

E2.justification: The main comparison remains OpenVLA AR against strict and relaxed Spec-VLA. Appendix C varies numerical precision within these methods rather than introducing another comparator algorithm. Newly discussed methods such as SEER, D3P and Kangaroo are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds inference-speed comparisons using bf16, int8 and int4 on an A100 80GB GPU. Table 5 normalizes OpenVLA speed against bf16; Table 6 names an OpenVLA AR baseline without explicitly identifying its precision. Settings for the original experiments are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C newly examines quantization-related slowdown and whether speculative decoding remains useful with quantized verification models. The threshold ablation, acceptance-length analyses and case study in Sections 5.2–6 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 trials per task for the main evaluation and 10 for the threshold sweep. Neither reports seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new quantization tables add point estimates without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–5 retain their results. Appendix C adds timing results: for LIBERO-Goal, Table 5 reports int8/int4 OpenVLA speed ratios of 0.24×/0.61× against bf16, while Table 6 reports 1.61×/1.34× for Spec-VLA against its stated AR baseline.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the action-token distance definition and the mathematical acceptance conditions are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs, and Appendix C adds no theoretical development.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims remain Spec-VLA's application of speculative decoding to VLA inference and distance-based relaxation yielding up to 44% longer acceptance and 1.42× speedup while preserving success rates. The revised introduction adds motivation for the existing robustness analysis.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly suggests that quantization overhead explains slower int8/int4 inference and presents speculative decoding as complementary to quantization. Existing interpretations of relaxation robustness and limitations concerning real-world robots and action chunking are retained.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a repository link and states that code and data are publicly available. Appendix C documents the tested precisions and timing hardware. Appendix A's hyperparameters and Appendix B's pseudocode are unchanged; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds reinforcement-learning robustness and efficiency connections, including SEER and D3P, plus Kangaroo and literature speedup comparisons in Section 2.2. It removes the Leviathan et al. (2023) citation. These additions broaden the background without redefining the main novelty position.

P1.justification: v2 adds short motivational and related-work passages, an availability sentence, acknowledgements and Appendix C, alongside small wording and punctuation edits. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 are enlarged while retaining their underlying content. Table 3 and Figure 5 shift placement, and Appendix C introduces Tables 5–6. The original table structures and figure designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix C adds useful deployment evidence about quantization slowdown and its interaction with speculative decoding. Repository access information and larger figures also improve usability. The gain is limited: the main validation is unchanged, and the new timing study omits task-success measurements and explicit baseline precision for Table 6.
